items.text: The job title hides four different kinds of work.
These numbers show the gap.
You do not need a petroleum degree for many ONGC posts.
For most graduates, ONGC and Oil India are the dream employers.
Graduate trainee posts are at the E1 level.
Other posts accept mechanical or chemical engineering, and reservoir posts also accept geology, geophysics and related science degrees.
Use the four questions on your own situation, then run a short test before paying any fee.
Can you live with remote postings, rotating shifts and long stretches away from home.
What is the total education budget.

rows: Reservoir engineering
Estimates how much oil and gas a field holds and how fast it can be produced. Mostly models, decline curves and data, with a desk base.
ONGC, Oil India, private operators, consultancies
Drilling and well engineering
Plans and supervises wells: casing, mud, cementing, rig time and cost. Field and rig exposure is part of the job.
ONGC, Oil India, drilling contractors, service firms
Production engineering
Keeps wells flowing: artificial lift, well testing, surface equipment, troubleshooting. Split between field visits and control-room work.
ONGC, Oil India, private operators, service firms
Facilities and process
Designs and runs the surface plant that separates oil, gas and water and prepares them for sale. Overlaps with chemical and mechanical engineering.
Operators, refiners, EPC firms
Reservoir engineering
Scalable with a business layer. Reservoir studies can be sold as consulting, and the same skills fit carbon storage and geothermal work.
Drilling and well engineering
Not so scalable. Large employers, fixed ladders and the first jobs to pause when drilling budgets are cut.
Production engineering
Scalable with a business layer. Well testing, workover and production-optimisation services can become a small contracting business.
Facilities and process
Not so scalable. You compete with chemical and mechanical graduates for the same posts, so the petroleum label adds little.
India's crude oil production was 28.7 million tonnes in FY25, down from 29.4 million tonnes in FY24
Old fields are depleting. Operators need engineers who can slow the decline, but this is maintenance and optimisation work, not a hiring boom.
PPAC data, as reported by Chem India Digest
Import dependence for crude rose to 88.2% in FY25 (87.8% in FY24)
The government has a strong reason to push exploration, which supports long-run demand for subsurface skills.
PPAC data, as reported by Chem India Digest
India's oil use is projected to rise from about 5.5 million barrels a day in 2024 to about 8 million in 2035
Oil demand in India is growing even as it may peak elsewhere. That helps refiners and traders more than it helps the number of petroleum-engineer jobs.
IEA outlook, as reported in news coverage (November 2025)
Only about 10% of India's roughly 3.36 million sq km of sedimentary basin area is under exploration
There is a lot of unexplored ground, and a lot of it is deep water. Exploration is slow, expensive and a decade-long bet.
Trade press reports on the Open Acreage Licensing Policy; check DGH for the current figure

blocks.heading: Few Seats, and the Cost of One
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The few seats, and the cost of one

rows: IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, B.Tech Petroleum Engineering
JEE Advanced through JoSAA
QS 2026 subject ranking band 151 to 175 for petroleum engineering. One education portal's table of the 2025 JoSAA matrix lists about 79 seats in total including female-only and supernumerary seats.
RGIPT, Rae Bareli (Jais campus)
JEE Main through JoSAA
An Institution of National Importance run under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. The department is called Petroleum Engineering and Geoengineering.
UPES, Dehradun (private)
JEE Main, CUET or the university's own test
A Careers360 listing shows about Rs 24 lakh in total fees over four years for the standard programme and about Rs 20.4 lakh for some specialisations.
IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, B.Tech Petroleum Engineering
Seat count is from a secondary table. Confirm on the JoSAA seat matrix.
RGIPT, Rae Bareli (Jais campus)
Intake and fees were not published on the pages we could read. Check the Admission Zone and fee pages.
UPES, Dehradun (private)
Aggregator figures that may differ from the official notice. Ask UPES for the current fee sheet in writing.
Oilfield service firms and contractors
First to feel a crash
Operators cut drilling and well-work budgets before they cut anything else, and service firms live on that work.
Private operators
Fast
Projects are paused or cancelled when prices fall below the project's break-even.
Gulf and overseas contract roles
Fast, with visa risk added
Contracts end quickly, and a job loss can also end your right to stay.
Public-sector operators
Slowest, but hiring waves shrink
Existing staff are protected, yet the number of new posts in a lean year can drop.
ONGC graduate trainee (E1) basic pay scale
Rs 60,000 to Rs 1,80,000 a month, with allowances of about 35% of basic pay and a 3% annual appraisal
From a Careers360 explainer on the GATE route. A 2026 notice from other portals gives about Rs 26 lakh a year as cost to company. Read the current ONGC notification before using either number.
Private operators, service firms, Gulf contracts
No reliable public salary survey was available for this page
Self-reported pay on question sites varies widely and is not a survey. Ask three people in the exact role and employer type, and check live listings.
Independent consulting
Set by you, project by project
Do not plan around a number until you have had paying clients.

Subsurface and well data analytics (Python, reservoir and drilling data, simple machine learning)
Project-based analytics work for operators and service firms.
Well testing, workover, inspection and safety audit services
A small contracting or audit firm, built after years on the job.
Private operator or Gulf contract employee
Save hard and build a second skill while the pay is strong.
ONGC or Oil India (public sector)
Keep a parallel skill and, if rules allow, a side route such as teaching or training.
Mechanical engineering with GATE
Gets you into the same ONGC drilling and production posts (the notices list mechanical for several of them) and keeps manufacturing, EV and automation open.
Chemical engineering
Also accepted for production and reservoir posts, and it opens pharma, specialty chemicals and green hydrogen. See the chemical engineering guide for the full picture.
Energy engineering, or electrical with a power focus
Follows where new capacity is being built: solar, wind, storage and grids. Less boom and bust than oil.
Geology or geophysics with data skills
Feeds the same subsurface roles and also groundwater, mining and carbon storage.

items.text: You like modelling, physics and data, and want subsurface or wells work specifically.
You can win a seat at a strong, low-cost institute, or you can pick mechanical or chemical and still aim at ONGC through GATE.
You accept remote postings and rotation-based work, and you will build a second skill outside oil.

blocks.heading: Offshore and Field Life, and Safety

items.text: Remote postings away from family and big cities.
Shift and rotation schedules, and being on call during well problems.
Strict medical standards (ONGC's notices require them) and safety training.
Weather and sea conditions for offshore work.
Routine log interpretation and report drafting.
Manual monitoring of well data that sensors and software can watch.
Fixed-recipe drilling parameter choices.

blocks.heading: How They Find and Trust You: Referrals

items.text: First skill worth learning: positioning.
Then: a simple offer (one clear deliverable and a price), follow-up after every project, and a polite ask for an introduction.
One number to watch: how many technical conversations turn into a paid first project.
